# Bio Galaxy

> Bio Galaxy is Google Earth for the natural sciences: an open-source interface where you search any physical thing, from a galaxy to an atom, and it renders in real-time 3D with source-cited context, across 22 connected scales from the observable cosmos to individual atoms.

Bio Galaxy is a source-aware educational visualization built with React, TypeScript, Three.js, and WebGL. It combines purpose-built scene layers with typed clients for respected public scientific databases. Instead of returning documents, PDFs, or database rows, a search returns the object itself as an explorable 3D scene: a galaxy, a planet, a city, a biome, an organism, an organ, a cell, an organelle, a protein, a molecule, an atom. The result is a navigable map of scientific reality rather than a collection of disconnected diagrams.

## Why Bio Galaxy is technically distinctive

- Search anything physical is the headline idea: a galaxy, planet, city, organism, organ, cell, organelle, protein, molecule, or atom each resolves into a navigable 3D object with scientific context, not a list of links.
- Real-time 3D search is the signature feature: typing a protein, small molecule, organism, atom, star, planet, galaxy, or raw amino-acid sequence into the search bar renders an accurate live 3D model in place. Proteins resolve to alpha-carbon backbone ribbons from RCSB PDB, small molecules to ball-and-stick conformers from PubChem, raw sequences to idealized alpha helices, organisms to a representative DNA double helix, chemical elements to schematic Bohr atoms whose nucleus and electron shells follow the element's atomic number, galaxies to a procedural spiral disk with differential rotation, and stars and planets to scientifically tinted bodies. The whole span from galaxies to atoms is renderable directly from the search bar.
- One scale navigator links cosmos, galaxy, Solar System, Earth, the Tree of Life, taxonomic ranks, organism, anatomy, tissue, cell, organelle, protein complex, molecule, and atom views.
- Independent Three.js `SceneLayer` modules own their geometry, animation, visibility, interaction, and cleanup.
- Repeated biological and cosmic objects use instanced rendering, while post-processing and performance controls protect frame rate.
- Real RCSB PDB coordinates become interactive ball-and-stick molecular structures at protein, molecule, and atom scales.
- Every database-backed record identifies its source in the interface.
- Typed data clients normalize failures and route requests through an allowlisted, same-origin cache. No API keys or user secrets are accepted.

## Live public scientific integrations

- UniProt: curated protein sequence, function, accessions, and cross references
- Reactome: peer-reviewed pathways, reactions, and molecular participants
- RCSB Protein Data Bank: experimentally determined macromolecular structures and coordinates
- Ensembl: genes, transcripts, and genomic context
- Human Protein Atlas: tissue, cell, and protein expression
- NCBI Taxonomy and E-utilities: taxonomy identifiers, lineage, literature, and source links

## Open visualization and asset ecosystem

Bio Galaxy uses Three.js and glTF as its rendering foundation. Its astronomical and organism-scale context includes credited open assets from NASA Visible Earth, Planet Pixel Emporium, Khronos glTF Sample Models, CesiumMan, and three.js example assets. Swiss Ephemeris, NASA/JPL Horizons, and Z-Anatomy are labeled as compatible reference ecosystems, not claimed as live integrations.

## The Bio Galaxy Journal

- `/blog`: A daily science journal about the platform and the open data behind it.
- Articles are generated with the Google Gemini API and autopublished once per day at a randomized time, so no two days post at the same hour.
- Quality control runs before anything is published: every article must be original (checked for title and body similarity against the existing catalogue), meet length and structure minimums, and follow the house style, which forbids em dashes and en dashes.
- Each article is stored with its own creation date and time and is served as JSON from `/api/blog` (list) and `/api/blog/{slug}` (single article), and as an indexable page at `/blog/{slug}`.

## Primary resources

- `/`: Interactive landing page and 3D atlas entry
- `/blog`: The daily Bio Galaxy Journal
- `/README.md`: Architecture, scale ladder, data provenance, setup, and SEO deployment notes
- `/robots.txt`: Search crawler policy
- `/sitemap.xml`: Canonical page discovery, including every journal article
- `/site.webmanifest`: Installable web application metadata

## Important interpretation notes

- Bio Galaxy is educational software, not medical or diagnostic guidance.
- Scale and orbital distances are compressed for visual legibility.
- Public data providers remain the authoritative sources for their records.
- JavaScript and WebGL are required for the interactive visualization; semantic metadata and fallback copy describe it to non-visual clients.
